awarding_body.value: Wound, Ostomy and Continence Nursing Certification Board (WOCNCB)

year_launched.note: Specific CWCN launch year not published by WOCNCB on public-facing pages.

eligibility.value: Active, unrestricted RN license in the US or its territories AND a Baccalaureate (BSN) or higher degree in nursing. Candidates choose ONE of two pathways: (1) Traditional Pathway - graduation from an accredited WOC Nursing Education Program (WOCNEP) within the past 5 years, OR (2) Experiential Pathway - completion of 50 CE hours in wound care plus 1,500 direct patient-care hours in wound care within the past 5 years, with at least 375 of those hours completed in the 12 months immediately preceding application.

exam_format.value: Computer-based exam delivered through PSI testing centers. 120 multiple-choice questions (110 scored + 10 unscored pretest items). 2-hour time limit. Offered year-round during a 6-month eligibility window after application approval.

passing_score.note: WOCNCB uses a 500 scaled passing score across its specialty exams; not a raw count.

fee.value: $395 USD for a single specialty exam application. Discounted bundles: 2 specialties $510, 3 specialties $610, 4 specialties $670. Failed first attempts receive a $100 discount on the next retake (one-time). Developing-country applicants may pay $100 per specialty.

renewal.value: Recertification is required every 5 years. Two pathways: (1) Re-take the certification exam, OR (2) Complete the Professional Growth Program (PGP) - submit an online portfolio totaling 80 PGP points, of which at least 10 must be continuing education hours in the clinical specialty (wound care). WOCNCB charges no annual maintenance fees.

salary_context.value: BLS-reported wound care nurse pay averages approximately $94,480/year (about $45.42/hour) with a lower-end of ~$63,720 and an upper-end near $132,680. Industry surveys: PayScale lists ~$85,000-$87,490 base; Indeed reports ~$99,434; ZipRecruiter reports ~$101,711. Outpatient care centers pay highest, averaging ~$102,640.

common_confusions.value: CWCN vs CWOCN: CWCN focuses solely on wound care; CWOCN (Certified Wound, Ostomy, and Continence Nurse) covers all three specialties. CWCN vs WCC: CWCN is WOCNCB-issued and requires a BSN; WCC (Wound Care Certified) is issued by the NAWCO and accepts a wider range of clinicians (RNs, LPNs, PTs, MDs). CWCN vs CWS: CWS (Certified Wound Specialist) is an interdisciplinary credential from the American Board of Wound Management for any healthcare professional with a bachelor's degree.

recent_changes.value: WOCNCB published an updated Detailed Content Outline in 2024 (effective for the 2024 exam cycle) reaffirming the five-domain blueprint with task-level weights for Assessment, Intervention, Treatment, Care Planning, and Education & Referral.

tasks: Assess comprehensive factors affecting wounds (7.55%, 8 items)
Obtain patient health history through interviews and records (7.17%, 8 items)
Perform focused assessments to determine skin status and wound etiology (8.82%, 10 items)
Recommend and/or provide appropriate interventions to promote optimal wound management (8.44%, 9 items)
Implement prevention measures to promote optimal skin health and prevent injury (8.11%, 9 items)
Recommend and/or perform wound bed preparation (7.43%, 8 items)
Recommend and/or perform debridement to promote wound healing (7.45%, 8 items)
Knowledge and application of topical therapies (7.52%, 8 items)
Knowledge and application of advanced/adjunctive therapies (7.10%, 8 items)
Develop a patient-centered plan of care using history and assessment (5.65%, 6 items)
Evaluate the patient-centered plan of care through periodic assessment (6.14%, 7 items)
Educate patients and caregivers using the individualized skin and wound care plan (6.57%, 7 items)
Educate other healthcare professionals on skin and wound care management (5.93%, 7 items)
Multidisciplinary care collaboration and referrals (6.13%, 7 items)

pass_rate_history.note: Reported via woundeducators.com summary of WOCNCB published statistics.

discrepancies.details: Mometrix cites a current pass rate of approximately 71%; woundeducators.com cites 68.3% for 2024 (1,417 candidates). Both are reported by third parties summarizing WOCNCB statistics.
